title: Mine, yours, his/hers: enyém, tiéd, övé

sections.title: Mine, yours, his/hers
sections.content: *kulcsom* is 'my key': a noun with an ending. When it is clear which thing you mean, Hungarian can use a word of its own instead of the ending on the noun, like English *mine*: *A kulcs az enyém.* (The key is mine.) The noun stays plain, and *az enyém* says whose it is. These words are *enyém* (mine), *tiéd* (yours) and *övé* (his/hers). They come after *az* or *a*: *az* before a vowel, *a* before a consonant. To ask 'whose?', say *kié*: *Kié a kulcs?*

English has two words, *my* and *mine*; Hungarian has two forms as well. *A kulcsom itt van* ('my key is here') puts the ending on the noun. *A kulcs az enyém* ('the key is mine') leaves the noun plain and lets the pronoun do the work. Use one or the other, not both.
